Preconditions: The test copy is running and you have its link. Accounts: Admin 900001, Department Head 940001, SAO 990001 (the SAO password the demo owner gave you). The password for the others comes from the tester sheet. A financial semester exists and the ledger has entries. Prepare a small PDF as a supporting file.
Steps:
1. Sign in as Admin 900001. Open Finance > Financial reports. Under "Prepare a report" choose "Financial Report", keep "Covered period" on Semester, type the four signatory names and select "Generate Financial Report".
2. In the list select "View details" on the draft and choose the PDF under "Supporting files".
3. Select "Submit for review" and read the stage.
4. Open Finance > Ledger and try "Edit transaction" on an entry that is in the report. Read the note.
5. Sign out. Sign in as Department Head 940001. Open Approvals, set Request type to Financial Report and select Review on the report.
6. Select Approve and confirm. Read the panel.
7. Sign out. Sign in as SAO 990001. Open Reviews > Compliance > Financial reports and select View on the report.
8. Select Approve and then "Approve report". Read the message.
9. Sign out. Sign in as Admin 900001. Open Finance > Financial reports and read the status. Open "View details" and look for "Submit for review".
10. Open Finance > Ledger and try again to edit or delete an entry that is in the report.
Expected result: After step 2 the stage is "Waiting for Department Head approval" and the ledger entries in the report are locked already (the note names the report). The Department Head's approval moves the report to the SAO. The SAO sees "Financial report approved." The Admin sees the report as Approved, with no "Submit for review" button, and the entries stay locked. An entry outside the report can still be edited.

Test case: SAO journeys: count the clicks against the limits
Depends on: Run with SAO-022, SAO-055, SAO-062, SAO-075 and SAO-014
Preconditions: The test copy is running and you have its link. Work in pairs: one person does the journey, one watches and writes. The watcher does not help. Sign in as SAO 990001 (the SAO password the demo owner gave you). Journey 1 needs a registration from a Department Head and an active semester (Round 2), and journey 5 needs a grievance addressed to the SAO. Start each journey at the home page after signing in. Typing and choosing a file do not count as clicks.
Steps:
1. Journey 1, approve a registration and give it an administrator: limit 5 clicks. End: the organization is Active with one administrator.
2. Journey 2, review compliance: limit 3 clicks. End: the submission shows its new status.
3. Journey 3, decide a financial report: limit 3 clicks. End: the report shows Approved.
4. Journey 4, see who needs attention: limit 2 clicks. End: organizations that need action are listed first.
5. Journey 5, answer a grievance: limit 4 clicks. End: the student's My grievances shows Resolved.
6. For each journey write the clicks you counted, whether the end state was reached, and any moment the person stopped and asked "where do I go now".
Expected result: Every journey reaches its end state within the limit and the person never asks where to go. A journey that needs more clicks, or where the person gets lost, is a finding: write it as "SAO, journey and step, what you did, what you expected, what happened" and mark it blocked, lost, wording or looks wrong (MEMBER_TESTING sections 4 and 7). Send blocked findings first.

Test case: Lost and wording findings for every role, and the menu label card sort
Depends on: Run after GEN-124, GEN-125, GEN-126, GEN-127 and GEN-128
Preconditions: The test copy is running and you have its link. Do this after the five role cases above. One tester per role (SAO, Department Head, Admin, Officer, Student) writes findings. Five student leaders who have not seen the menu do the card sort (10 minutes).
Steps:
1. Each tester answers these five questions for their role: Where did I not know what to do next? Which word did I not understand and what did I think it meant? Where did I click and get another result than I expected? Which page did I want but could not find in the menu? Did two screens disagree about the same thing, for example a status?
2. Write one line per finding: Role, journey and step, what you did, what you expected, what happened, screenshot if any.
3. Mark each line: blocked (could not finish), lost (finished but confused), wording (misleading text) or looks wrong (layout or visual).
4. Card sort: give five student leaders one card for each page name (without the groups). Ask them to group the cards and give each group a name. Compare their groups and names with the menu groups Records, Events and tasks, Store and Updates.
5. List every difference between their groups and the menu as a finding. Send blocked findings first.
Expected result: Each role has a list of findings in the one-line shape, each marked blocked, lost, wording or looks wrong, with blocked ones sent first. The card sort gives a list of differences between the leaders' groups and names and the menu. A role with no findings says "no lost moments, no confusing words" in writing.
